item.title: ‘Too early for him’: Sachin Tendulkar's blunt verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s leadership role at 15
item.description: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers. From finishing as the leading run-scorer in an Indian Premier League (IPL) season to smashing a match-winning century in the U-19 World Cup final to clinch the title, the teenager has made remarkable strides in a short span of time. However, his elevation to the role of East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy did not go down well with everyone. Among those who believe the youngster was handed a leadership responsibility too early is batting legend Sachin Tendulkar. Although Tendulkar had not publicly questioned the selectors' decision at the time of the announcement, he shared his reservations during a Reddit Q&A session, suggesting that Sooryavanshi should focus on gaining more experience in red-ball cricket before taking on such responsibilities. Responding to a fan who asked for his views on the 15-year-old being entrusted with a leadership role, Tendulkar said: "I feel it's too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!" Sooryavanshi had featured in just eight red-ball matches for Bihar before being named East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan's deputy. The decision meant he was preferred over Abhimanyu Easwaran, an experienced campaigner with more than 100 First-Class appearances. The East Zone selection committee subsequently clarified that the appointment was made with the youngster's development in mind and should not be interpreted as an indication of the pecking order within the squad. Sooryavanshi also got a taste of captaincy during the tournament when Kishan was forced to leave the field due to an injury. The teenager stepped in to lead the side and was involved in several important on-field decisions, including DRS calls. Videos of his involvement in those reviews also gained traction on social media. Meanwhile, Sooryavanshi has continued to strengthen his position in India's T20I setup, although he is yet to establish himself as a regular opener. The youngster faces competition for a place in the top three from established names such as Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan. item.title: Bayern assistant Danks: Kompany recovering well but no return yet
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany (R) and assistant coach Aaron Danks walk across the field ahead of the German Bundesliga championship trophy ahead of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and VfB Stuttgart at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern assistant Danks: Kompany recovering well but no return yet») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is making progress in his recovery ahead of the team's away match in Mainz, assistant coach Aaron Danks said at a press conference on Friday. Danks could not yet say whether the 40-year-old Belgian could resume his role as coach of the German football record champions after his collapse two weeks earlier and a bout of meningitis following the international break. "I've had a few really good phone calls with Vince. He seems very positive and appears to be well on the way to a full recovery," Danks said. The assistant coach added that no date has been set yet for Kompany's return. "The international break provides a good opportunity to reflect and see when he can return," he said, adding that everyone hopes that it will be as soon as possible. Under the guidance of Kompany's assistant Danks, Bayern have won three and drawn one of their last four competitive matches. Another win could follow on Saturday in Mainz, where Bayern suffered their last away defeat, a 2-1 loss in December 2024. Since then, Bayern have gone 30 away matches unbeaten, recording 22 wins and eight draws. "We've got an important match on Saturday, and we want to round off this run with a good result. But it won't be easy. We know that," Danks said. Four days after the 2-0 Champions League win at Atlético Madrid, there could be changes to the starting line-up. "With a few players we need to look at workload and whether we rest them," Danks said. Danks named Alphonso Davies, who still needs rest periods after several injuries, and said he could not play 90 minutes in a row several times. Germany international Jamal Musiala is back in team training after his muscle injury. "But tomorrow's game comes too soon for him," Danks added.

item.title: Audrey Shindelar shines in SDSU debut, sets program debut scoring mark
item.description: South Dakota State true freshman Audrey Shindelar poured in 15 points on Tuesday, Nov. 2, setting the program's Division I record for points in a debut outing. Shindelar scored her 15 points in 22 minutes, going 7-for-11 from the field and 1-for-3 from three. She looked confident getting to her shot in both the half-court and on the break. "I trust my preparation and my teammates and coaches, I knew they had my back," Shindelar said. "I went in the game with confidence in what we had been working on." The freshman guard isn't normally a nervous person, but she was feeling the pressure a little before her first collegiate game. She was able to channel that positively and give her team a lift. "I'm not usually a very nervous person, but being in a new setting and in a little bit of the unknown," Shindelar said. "Before games there's just a different schedule and that kind of stuff. Then a lot of people were there supporting. It was really cool and it was good nerves." Shindelar's coaches and teammates weren't at all shocked at her performance. Shindelar is the all-time leading scorer at Stewartville High School in southeast Minnesota. She was also a Miss Basketball finalist in Minnesota a year ago. "Honestly, we're not surprised," SDSU guard Emilee Fox said after Tuesday's game. "Audrey's a really good player and we're really excited to see how she can progress each and every game." Head coach Aaron Johnston expected her to come in and contribute immediately, and is happy his freshman guard is succeeding early. He's going to be sure he isn't adding too much pressure to Shindelar as she continues getting adapted to the grind of a college season. "You never know how freshmen are going to jump into things," Johnston said. "It's hard going from a senior in high school to the freshman year in college against our level of competition. We want to make sure we don't put too much on her, but she's going to be a big part of what we do from Day 1 and going forward because she has the ability to create shots and has really good bounce in her step. She's going to be a great talent for us." Shindelar is hoping her opening performance can carry on in the season. She's just hoping that will result in some team wins after the Jackrabbits lost to Creighton at the buzzer. "The loss was tough, but I feel like consistency is a big part for everybody," Shindelar said. "I feel like that's an important piece in getting better every day in practice, every game." item.description: Rose Lavelle (Gotham), Croix Bethune (Kansas City) and Trinity Rodman (Washington) are among the stars seeking to lead their team to an NWSL title. Composite: Photo by Elsa/NWSL via Getty Images; Lachlan Cunningham/NWSL via Getty Images; Greg Fiume/Getty Images The regular season was defined by … Compelling storylines that kept the league interesting during a crowded sports summer. The interval years that aren’t Olympic or World Cup years are often quieter for the NWSL (see: average attendance was essentially flat among the non-expansion teams). In a year with the men’s World Cup on home soil and a major anniversary season for the WNBA, most of the NWSL’s teams gave a solid showing, with close competition for the Shield, an entertaining Golden Boot race and the returns of several big stars. Even those teams who did not give a solid showing – hello, Chicago – finally made some encouraging moves in the right direction. (Louisville next, please.) Ella Brockway The league working to gauge the heart of its fanbase. Recent weeks have seen contentious scenes, especially in Portland, as transphobic organizations try to work into the league discourse as they have with the WNBA. But beyond that, there have been considerable innovations made with an eye on garnering more attention. The “Rodman Rule” was hurried to production in part to keep arguably the most marketable US player from going abroad. The league briefly considered following MLS’s lead and inverting its schedule, only for a vote to be spurned after initial backlash from players and the public. It even got a feature in Ted Lasso. These efforts take time, but that’s a lot of willingness to change just about anything about the league’s structure if it moves the needle. Jeff Rueter Races to the top – and the bottom. The competition for both the Shield and Golden Boot was fierce. Ashley Sanchez pulled ahead for the Boot, but Barbra Banda, Sophia Wilson, Janine Sonis and Trinity Rodman provided some real fireworks. (Had Banda not been kept out of the country for the last month of games due to federal travel policies, she may have given Sanchez a run for her money.) The Shield race was even tighter, with three teams still in contention with two matches to go. However, the league struggled to maintain that quality across the board. Chicago, Louisville and Bay FC were embarrassingly bad – and boring – throughout the season. It’s a story that is too familiar, and doesn’t seem poised to change in a real way any time soon. As much as the league’s marketing centers parity, its choices prioritize expansion. With two new clubs arriving in 2028 and more on the way after, I worry the talent across the board will continue to be watered down, especially as the league’s salary cap and low minimum salary drives elite players away to teams in Europe, Mexico and Brazil. item.title: Kimi Antonelli on Having His Dad at ‘99% of the Races’ as Life ‘Changed Drastically’
item.description: When you become the youngest Formula 1 World Champion in history at just 20 years old, it is terrifyingly easy to lose your grip on reality. Replacing a seven-time champion at Mercedes , dominating the grid, and suddenly becoming the most famous athlete in Italy is the kind of explosive spotlight that can completely break a young driver. So, how did Kimi Antonelli manage to keep his head screwed on straight while the F1 circus went into absolute overdrive around him? He brought his dad to work. Speaking with Anthony Davidson on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show , Antonelli peeled back the curtain on his inner circle. When asked who helped him survive the immense pressure and the difficult moments of his early career, the Mercedes star immediately pointed to his father, Marco Antonelli. Marco is no stranger to the brutal realities of the motorsport ecosystem. As a former racing driver himself and the boss of the AKM Motorsport outfit, he understands exactly how toxic the paddock can get. Having that veteran presence in his corner was the ultimate cheat code for the young champion. “First of all, my family, of course my dad, my mom, but my family in general, because they’re the ones who know me the best, inside out, and they’ve always been there for me, especially my dad coming to the races,” Antonelli explained. Antonelli on Surviving the “Drastic” Fame While Antonelli has projected an icy, unshakable composure inside the cockpit of the W17 this season, he didn’t sugarcoat the psychological toll of the 2026 campaign. Going from a highly touted rookie to a global superstar essentially overnight completely upended his normal reality. He heavily relied on his father to act as a shield against the paddock noise. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) “I know I can rely on him any time. That has made a difference even this year,” Antonelli confessed. “This year, having my dad there 99% of the races has been massively helpful, because it’s been such a big year for me so far that I needed that support from him to cope with all the different situations, to cope as well with all these high moments, because life has changed drastically as well this year”. item.title: Why Soccer’s Major Tournaments Are Rethinking Opening Acts
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JULY 6: Edson Alvarez of Mexico and Guillermo Ochoa of Mexico lift the Gold Cup trophy with team mates during the Gold Cup 2025 Final match between United States and Mexico at NRG Stadium on July 6, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) Getty Images For years, the traditional opening stages of major soccer tournaments have followed a familiar script: Group-stage games, a handful of predictable mismatches and the gradual build toward the heavyweight encounters that everyone really wants to see. That approach is changing. From UEFA’s revamped Champions League (now in its third year) to the significant restructuring of the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup, the game’s governing bodies are rethinking how their competitions begin with a common objective: Get the biggest teams playing more meaningful games against one another earlier in the tournament. There are differences between the Champions League and Gold Cup approaches. Nonetheless, both are responding to the same challenge: Making the opening stage feel like an essential part of the tournament rather than an obstacle to the games that really matter. The traditional group stage was designed around simplicity and familiarity. Instead, these newer models are designed around variety, competitive incentives and commercial appeal. Overall, the thinking is straightforward. Why make fans wait until the knockout rounds to see the most compelling matches when those games can become part of the opening act? The most prominent example is the Champions League, which introduced its expanded league-phase format in the 2024-25 season. Gone was the familiar arrangement of 32 clubs divided into eight groups of four, with each team playing three opponents twice. In its place came a 36-team competition in which every club plays eight different opponents – four at home and four away – in one overarching league table. The change was designed to produce more variety, more competitive balance and, crucially, more heavyweight encounters during the fall. That means supporters can see some of Europe’s biggest clubs take on each other ahead of the knockout stage. It also creates a more compelling competitive landscape, with every result affecting a shared table. There is also considerably more at stake throughout the opening phase. The top eight teams qualify directly to the round of 16, while clubs finishing between ninth and 24th enter a two-legged playoff. Those finishing 25th or lower are eliminated. As a result, the league phase is not simply an extended qualifying exercise. A team’s position can determine whether it enjoys a direct route to the last-16. item.title: How 14-Game Road Nonleague Schedule Benefits Mississippi Valley State
item.description: Former University of Albany forward Tarique Foster now plays at Mississippi Valley State, which is playing each of its 14 nonconference games on the road. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Images Mike Davis isn’t naïve. The first-year men’s basketball coach at Mississippi Valley State University knows his team is facing a challenging first two months of the season, maybe more so than any program in the nation. The Delta Devils are last among 365 Division 1 teams in analyst Ken Pomeroy’s ratings. Still, MVSU is playing each of its 14 nonconference games on the road, starting with Friday’s opener at Oklahoma. The Delta Devils face five teams that were in the 2026 NCAA tournament and four that are ranked in the Associated Press preseason poll in No. 4 Connecticut, No. 12 Arkansas, No. 16 Michigan and No. 19 Texas Tech. KenPom projects MVSU will lose each of the nonleague games by at least 21 points. And that doesn’t bother Davis. Not at all. In fact, Davis assembled the schedule soon after he took over MVSU in early May. The reasoning is two-fold. MVSU expects to earn about $1.5 million in revenue by playing these games, a massive figure for a school of its standing in the low-major Southwestern Athletic Conference. The Delta Devils also can test themselves against high-major programs, which may help them in conference play. During the 2024-25 school year, the most recent data available, MVSU’s athletics department generated $5.58 million in revenue, including $993,877 from the men’s basketball team, per the U.S. Department of Education’s database. By playing a difficult schedule, the men’s basketball team can add significant funds to the school’s financial coffers because major conference teams pay appearance fees to smaller schools that travel to their arenas. MVSU will receive an average of $110,000 per game for its nonconference games this season, according to athletics director Alecia Shields-Gadson. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) Getty Images In mid-October, ESPN’s Zach Kram published his latest NBA Now or Later rankings , which gauge the teams that are under the most pressure to win right away. The rankings are based on how much money each team has tied up moving forward and their future first-round picks (or lack thereof). The Phoenix Suns led the way, as they’ve traded away four fully unprotected first-round picks over the next seven years and have given up swap rights in 2028 and 2030 as well. But the Cleveland Cavaliers were right behind them at No. 2 overall in ESPN’s rankings. The Cavs aren’t as overleveraged as the Suns in terms of future draft capital. They already owe their fully unprotected 2027, 2029 and 2031 first-round picks to other teams, and they’ve given up swap rights in 2028 as well. But for now, they have full control over their 2030, 2032 and 2033 first-rounders, whereas Phoenix only has control over its 2032 pick. What the Cavs don’t have is financial flexibility moving forward. The Suns have Devin Booker locked up on a 35% max contract, but they don’t have any massive long-term commitments beyond that. The Cavaliers can’t say the same. They just signed Donovan Mitchell to a 35% max deal, have Evan Mobley entering the second year of a 30% max and signed James Harden to a three-year, $96.5 million contract and added Peyton Watson on a four-year, $88 million deal via sign-and-trade this offseason. Throw in Jarrett Allen, who’s beginning a three-year, $90.7 million contract this season, and the Cavaliers have five players earning at least $20 million, three earning at least $30 million and two earning $50.1 million each. Next year, Mobley and Mitchell are projected to earn roughly $115 million combined, while Harden and Allen account for another $62.4 million. That quartet alone will push the Cavs over the 2027-28 salary cap, which is currently projected to land at $176 million . That’s setting this up to be a make-or-break season for the Cavaliers. If they fall short of the NBA Finals yet again, they may find it financially unsustainable to keep this core together moving forward. Can This Cavs Core Break Through? Eight games into the 2026-27 season, the Cavs have already shown a few red flags. In their season opener, they jumped out to a 29-point first-half lead over the Philadelphia 76ers and still managed to lose. item.title: SPL boss makes damning observation about Man United’s Jekyll and Hyde performance vs AS Roma
item.description: SPL boss makes damning observation about Man United’s Jekyll and Hyde performance vs AS Roma Dundee manager Steven Pressley has revealed what he told his players after Manchester United’s dramatic comeback against AS Roma, a message Michael Carrick’s men ought to take note of. Sensational turnaround United have made a dreadful start to the 2026/27 campaign, and their woeful sequence looked set to persist earlier this week in their meeting with Roma. The Red Devils found themselves 2-0 down inside 17 minutes, with Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen finding the back of the net. Both goals came about as a result of extremely poor defending. United received a lifeline on the hour mark via Bruno Fernandes’s penalty conversion. Having missed his initial attempt, he was granted a second bite of the apple due to an encroachment offence, and he duly made no mistake at the second time of asking. The hosts huffed and puffed and eventually restored parity in the 83rd minute when Matheus Cunha pounced on a missed clearance to fire home from close range. Cunha completed the turnaround three minutes later, connecting with a sublime pass from Shea Lacey and hammering home from a tight angle. The Brazilian was then sent off in stoppage time for a needless challenge on Leonardo Balerdi. United held on for all three points and a much-needed confidence boost. The difference between the first half and the second was immense. United appeared dead and buried in the first half, delivering a miserable performance that has become all too familiar this season. But in the second, they were almost a different side and Roma could not cope with them. This did not go unnoticed by Pressley, who observed that United simply exerted more effort and covered more ground, a message he conveyed to his players. Telling message The Dundee gaffer told The Courier , “I spoke to the group and asked them had they seen the Manchester United game.” “Because everyone loves to talk about tactics but then I watch that game and I see a team losing 2-0 at half time and what was the change?” He added, “They ran harder in the second half, they played with more energy.” “Of course tactics is important, I’m not disregarding that, but I think that we can never underestimate that if you want to win football games you have to do the basics of the game very well.” “Just now we have a league where the margins are so fine and if you don’t do the basics, if you don’t outrun your opponent, if you don’t win your duels, you don’t win games.” United are next in action on Sunday when they host Aston Villa .

While Smithson Valley's varsity squad practices outside in the mornings, freshmen practice begins at 3:30 p.m. To comply with UIL's heat safety rules, including the new wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) rule that went into effect in August, Smithson Valley head coach Larry Hill has occasionally modified how his freshmen practice. "Sometimes it's as simple as moving it from the turf to the grass because the temperature over there is obviously cooler," Hill said. "Other times, even on the grass it's too hot. So you know whether it's taking breaks or practice in shorts, [we'll do] whatever the mandate calls for." Escaping the heat This is the third story in a multi-part series on the UIL's new mandatory requirement of wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) measurements as part of an effort to combat heat across the state. Next: How a few districts are moving junior high games to the winter to protect their students While moving practice from an artificial turf field to a natural grass field does keep players cooler, why is that the case? "High schools are now switching to sport turf, and the underlying surface of sport turf oftentimes is ground-up automobile tires, so black and rubber, and it gets hot, and it radiates that heat back up onto the participant," Dr. Bud Cooper, clinical professor emeritus in the University of Georgia's department of kinesiology Cooper said. "So you know, we have to be really concerned about that." The ground absorbs heat and reflects it back onto the person, Cooper added. That's why standing outside on a grass lawn in the summer doesn't feel as hot as standing on a black asphalt parking lot. A study conducted by Penn State University in 2004 found that under direct sunlight exposure, surface temperatures of synthetic turf can be significantly higher than that of natural grass, sometimes as much as 35 to 55 degrees hotter. But just by using WBGT readings, schools are technically already taking surface heat conditions into account. Cooper explained WBGT readings factor in black globe, or radiant heat, temperatures. "That's the effects of the sun on your surroundings," Cooper said. At the same time, the Rams are a talented and well-coached team, having blown out the Giants 28-6 in Week 2 and the Chargers 24-9 last week. On offense, the Rams are coached by head coach Sean McVay, offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, and assistant HC Kliff Kingsbury, with McVay calling the plays. Two of those three coaches should be familiar to Washington fans as they were former playcallers here. This offense is built around one of the NFL’s best offensive lines , a gap-scheme run game that favors power, and the NFL’s highest use of 3-TE sets . It’s an offense that sets up to bludgeon opposing defenses in the run game, but also uses their heavy personnel tendency to force opposing defenses to go heavy and set up star WR Puka Nacua to feast on heavier, slower defensive matchups. This kind of offense funnels the ball to Nacua, who currently leads the NFL with a 37.9% target share . A ruptured hamstring by WR Davante Adams will only increase the likelihood of the Rams going heavy and throwing the ball to Nacua. Overall, the Rams have the 3rd-ranked passing offense and the 6th-ranked rushing offense in terms of yards per game. On defense, the Rams have been led by DC Chris Shula, who has worked his way up from being the assistant linebackers coach of the Rams in 2017. Shula has typically employed a 3-4 front with heavy use of zone coverage on the backend, though he is also known for extensive use of disguise, both on his pressure packages (faking a blitz from one direction while actually bringing pressure from another), and in his coverage (rotating coverages post-snap to confuse QBs). This year, after the Rams traded a 1st-round pick for shutdown CB Trent McDuffie, they have occasionally been using him to shadow star WRs, which allowed him to erase Malik Nabers in their Week 2 matchup. However, McDuffie’s status is uncertain this week after sustaining a back injury against the Chargers. The Rams also just lost star CB Jaylen Watson to a season-ending shoulder injury, which could leave the backend of the Rams defense weakened. At the same time, Los Angeles may be getting back star pass rusher Myles Garrett this week, which would be a tremendous boon for their defense. Overall, the Rams have run one of the NFL’s best defenses this year by many metrics, though it has ranked better against the pass (7th) than run (15th) . (Photo by Alex Zadorozny/MLB Photos via Getty Images) MLB Photos via Getty Images Before next season begins, the Toronto Blue Jays have several important decisions to make as regarding the rotation. After trading away Kevin Gausman and with a free agent decision looming over Shane Bieber, the team is likely to bolster the pitching staff with another arm. That could push the team to strike a reunion with future Hall of Fame righty Max Scherzer, unless he hangs up his spikes first. Shortly before his final start for the Blue Jays in this past season, Scherzer told reporters that he was not sure whether he would seek to continue his career and that he wouldn’t rush into a decision. “If he pitches, he could join a team in camp or even kick it down the road a bit longer, waiting for the perfect situation early in the season or midway through,” Keegan Matheson wrote for MLB.com at the time. “For now, Scherzer insists that this is all still up in the air.” Now Scherzer has provided his first update on his pitching plans since the season ended. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees’ 25-Year-Old Depth Pitcher Cuts Ties With Team After Major Injury Toronto Blue Jays Free Agent Max Scherzer Sends Return Update Ahead Of Potential MLB Lockout On Thursday, Scherzer indicated that a return is still on the table as he detailed his workout plans for an inevitable labor lockout next month. “Future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer, 42, might keep pitching, and if his boffo finale in Toronto on short rest is any indication, there’s more there,” according to the New York Post’s Jon Heyman . “He tells The Post he plans to pitch in ‘lockout games’ near his Florida home, which will give him a better idea if season 20 will happen.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Blue Jays Respond To Anthony Santander’s Anti-Muslim Social Media Posts Toronto Blue Jays Could Reunite With Max Scherzer Following Lockout Announcement Although his time with the Blue Jays has included some injury setbacks, Scherzer’s contributions to the team’s postseason run in 2025 helped cement his place in the organization’s recent history. And his latest comments suggest that his playing career might not be finished just yet. Assuming his performance in the lockout games goes well, in the same form with which he finished the season, Scherzer could appeal to the Blue Jays as a mid-rotation reunion. item.title: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Northwestern Wildcats Game Preview
item.description: This Saturday, the 6-2 Iowa Hawkeyes travel to the new Ryan Field to take on the surprisingly competitive 6-2 Northwestern Wildcats. The winner of this matchup keeps their (slim) playoff hopes alive while the loser will be left with a consolation-prize bowl game. Iowa beat Michigan, but even though I think Michigan played Iowa well, my opinion doesn’t count, and the Michigan win won’t impress the playoff committee. Wisconsin is good…on defense. Washington and Iowa State: eh. Looking forward, Illinois and Purdue aren’t impressive and Nebraska…well, I wouldn’t get my hopes up. That means this is Iowa’s last chance for a statement win. With a win in Evanston, the Hawks have a shot, albeit a distant one, of making the playoffs. Everything is on the line, but then again, everything was on the line in Minnesota too. 3 Questions Can Iowa Contain Aidan Chiles? Aidan Chiles is one of two quarterbacks on Iowa’s schedule that it has faced before—the other was Drake Lindsay—although when the Hawkeyes played Chiles, he was playing for Michigan State. That was in 2024 at which time Chiles had all the talent in the world but was highly inconsistent. Except against Iowa in which he had his best game of 2024 and Iowa lost a game it had no business losing to a MSU team that finished 5-7. Fast forward two years and Aidan Chiles is now a Wildcat and is the model of efficiency and consistency. He is currently completing 68.8% of his passes for 9.4 yards-per-attempt. He has thrown 13 touchdowns to 1 interception. He has also rushed for 274 yards, 10 touchdowns and 3.2 yards-per-carry. He is, after OSU’s Julian Sayin, the best quarterback Iowa will face this season. He might even be better than Sayin; Chiles is more dynamic, and he doesn’t have a safety valve named Jeremiah Smith. To make matters worse, NU boasts a strong rushing attack that will keep defenses honest, two very good tight ends, and the top wide receiver, Griffin Wilde, has 44 receptions and is averaging a whopping 17.3 yards-per-catch. In short, Iowa can’t just spy Chiles and hope that takes care of it. The Cats scored 23 points against Indiana, the best defense they have faced. Those 23 points were the most anyone, including Ohio State, has scored on the Hoosiers this year. It is worth noting that Northwestern was getting shut out until the second half. In the first half, the Hoosiers limited the big plays, kept everything in front of them and didn’t let Chiles out of the pocket. In the second half, to put it bluntly, they didn’t do those things. It’s a standard Phil Parker gameplan. Make them drive the field. Don’t let them get the big plays. Keep the quarterback in the pocket. Tighten up in the red zone. Iowa is unlikely to shut down the Cats’ high-powered offense, but if they can limit it, make them settle for field goals, win the field-position battle, and the offense can do its part then the Hawks can walk out of Evanston with a win. item.title: Drake Maye’s early-season turnaround earns him October honors
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots throws a pass against the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. The award comes after Maye led the Patriots to a 3-1 record, completing 67.2% of his passes for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He also added 129 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Maye became the first Patriot to earn the honor since Tom Brady during the 2017 season. “That’s something to be proud of for Drake,” Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “I always look at those things as team achievements. Certainly nobody’s going to win an individual award in football without all the guys that do their jobs around him. I think you celebrate that as a group. “He’s certainly deserving of it, and a lot of credit to him for just kind of improving as September finished and got into the next month of the season. A lot of little things he did better, and hopefully we can continue to do that.” It marked a significant turnaround for Maye after the 24-year-old struggled to open the season. The quarterback was perhaps the biggest reason the Patriots found themselves with a 1-2 record through the first three weeks, throwing just one touchdown against six interceptions. Improved ball security has been one of the biggest factors in Maye’s resurgence. He has thrown just one interception over the last four weeks, while his 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate in October ranked third among qualified quarterbacks. Additionally, Maye’s trademark deep ball has returned despite the Patriots losing several of their top pass catchers to injuries, while has has operated as one of the league’s better quarterbacks when dealing with pressure. “He has worked really diligently for two years now on becoming a better passer from the pocket,” McDaniels said. “Everybody talks about how his athleticism is, and it’s great, and he made another great play outside the pocket last week. But I’d say he’d probably be more excited about the one that he slid to the right and climbed up into the pocket, and makes the throw down the field to Kyle [Williams]. So I think he’s worked really hard at it. “I think it’s repetition and I think it’s confidence in the protections. I think that’s where it stems from.” Maye’s November started strong as well as he scored three total touchdowns to lead a come from behind win in Miami. The quarterback will look to keep things going against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday.
